definition: A structured or semi-structured repository of information that an AI system can query or retrieve from to ground its responses.
details: Knowledge bases used in RAG systems can range from simple document collections to structured databases or knowledge graphs, providing a source of truth beyond what's encoded in a model's parameters.

explainer.lead: A knowledge base is a structured or semi-structured store of information an AI system can query or retrieve from to ground its answers. It matters because it grounds responses in a source of truth beyond what is baked into the model's parameters.

tiers.eli5: It is like a reference shelf the AI can look things up in instead of relying only on memory.
tiers.practitioner: In RAG systems engineers point retrieval at a knowledge base, which may be a document collection, a structured database or a knowledge graph. A pitfall is that grounding quality depends on what the knowledge base actually contains.
tiers.paperLevel: A knowledge base is a structured or semi-structured repository of information that an AI system can query or retrieve from. Its forms range from document collections to structured databases and knowledge graphs.

explainer.example: A RAG system retrieves passages from a document collection acting as its knowledge base before generating an answer.
